newsitem.title: MEXICO: Chase unit finances Mexican wastewater plant.
newsitem.headline: Chase unit finances Mexican wastewater plant.

text.p: Chase Securities Inc's Global Power and Environmental Group said Tuesday that it has completed the second non-recourse financing in Latin America to build a wastewater-treatment plant -- the Cadereyta facility in Mexico's northern Nuevo Leon state.
The deal is the first project financing to take uncovered Mexican political risk since the peso crisis in December 1994, Chase said in a news release.
Chase also said it was the adviser and arranger for Latin America's first wastewater treatment project financed on a non-recourse basis, Mexico's Chihuahua Norte project.
Chase has been an adviser to Cydsa SA on the Cadereyta project since 1994, the press release said.

Cydsa's wholly owned environmental subsidiary, Grupo Empresarial de Mejoramiento Ambiental (Gema), was awarded the $33.4 million Caderyeta project by Petroleos Mexicanos, or Pemex, the state-owned oil and gas monopoly.
The project aims to treat some 14 million gallons of water per day and achieve "zero discharge" from the refinery. Treated water will be returned to the refinery for reuse.

Chase said it was the arranger and underwriter of $24 million in non-recourse financing with a total term of 10 years for construction and operation of the Cadereyta project, noting that its willingness to underwrite the deal was due to the creditworthiness of the off-taker, Pemex.

Pemex also has plans to build wastewater treatment plants at four other refineries in Madero, Minatitlan, Salina Cruz and Tula. Chase said it is the financial adviser and arranger for the Madero project.
